themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaint Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints exploded to 5 this week versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,900% spike (z-score: 14.74)—suggesting rapid expansion of street seating or enforcement complaints tied to the Goop ghost kitchen opening on April 17th.
evidence: 5 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3,900% increase)
Gothamist reported Goop ghost kitchen opening at Carroll Street on April 17, 2026—same timeframe as spike onset
Z-score of 14.74 indicates extreme statistical deviation from baseline
reporting_angles: Is the new ghost kitchen operating with proper permits and compliance? Interview CB and DOE about outdoor dining regulations.
Are residents complaining about foot traffic, noise, or blocked sidewalks from the new dining setup? Canvass the immediate neighborhood.

themes_detail.label: Encampment Complaints Triple
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints spiked to 8 this week compared to a 1.8 weekly baseline (357% increase, z-score: 3.81), signaling a potential homelessness crisis in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens that mirrors the Community Board's repeated budget requests for homeless services.
evidence: 8 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (357% spike)
Z-score of 3.81 indicates statistically significant deviation
Community Board has submitted recurring budget requests for 'Other services for the homeless' to Department of Homeless Services—showing this is a persistent, unresolved district concern
reporting_angles: Where are encampments concentrated? Map complaints and interview affected residents, business owners, and homeless services providers.
Why has DHS not responded to the Community Board's recurring budget requests? Interview CB members and DHS about resource allocation.
What services exist in the district and are they adequate? Profile local nonprofits and capacity gaps.

themes_detail.label: Maintenance & Facilities Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints jumped to 22 this week versus a 6.0 weekly baseline (267% increase, z-score: 5.49), indicating potential deterioration of public infrastructure, parks, or city-owned buildings across the district.
evidence: 22 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs 6.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (267% increase)
Z-score of 5.49 indicates strong statistical significance
Community Board budget requests include park reconstruction, senior center renovation, and park safety enhancements—suggesting systemic neglect
reporting_angles: What specific facilities are failing? Pull 311 complaint details to identify buildings, parks, or infrastructure types most affected.
Are Prospect Park, Commodore Barry Park, or other major district amenities underfunded? Inspect and interview Parks Department.

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints quintupled to 5 this week versus a 1.0 weekly baseline (400% increase, z-score: 3.58), and overgrown tree/branch complaints hit 7 last week versus 1.6 average (331% increase, z-score: 5.42), suggesting widespread tree canopy stress in the district.
evidence: 5 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.0 weekly average (400% spike, z-score: 3.58)
7 overgrown tree/branch complaints last week vs 1.6 weekly average (331% spike, z-score: 5.42)
329 damaged tree complaints total over 90 days shows chronic tree stress; combined spikes suggest acute environmental trigger (disease, drought, storm damage)
reporting_angles: Have recent weather events (drought, heavy rain, high winds) stressed the tree canopy? Consult Parks Department forestry data.
Is there a specific pest or disease affecting district trees? Interview NYC Parks arborists and environmental groups.
Are tree maintenance budgets adequate? Cross-check Parks funding with CB budget requests.

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Safety Hazard
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street sign complaints peaked at 5 three weeks ago versus a 0.6 weekly baseline (700% increase, z-score: 6.29), indicating potential public safety risk from deteriorating traffic infrastructure that requires urgent city intervention.
evidence: 5 dangling street sign complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs 0.6 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 6.29)
High z-score indicates sustained outlier status
Traffic signal condition also in top 10 311 complaints (326 over 90 days), suggesting broader traffic infrastructure decay
reporting_angles: Which street segments have dangling signs? Conduct visual audit and identify safety hazards for pedestrians and vehicles.
Has DOT responded to repair requests? File FOIL for 311-to-DOT response data and timelines.
Is this part of a larger pattern of deferred maintenance? Compare sign complaints to broader DOT budget constraints.
